newsitem.title: HONG KONG: SAS to add fifth Hong Kong frequency.
newsitem.headline: SAS to add fifth Hong Kong frequency.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System ) is to add a fifth weekly frequency to its Hong Kong-Copenhagen non-stop schedule from April 4 because of increased demand, said Per Moller Jensen, the airline's general manager for Hong Kong, Macau, South China, Taipei and the Philippines.
SAS also has plans to increase the service to daily frequency, but not until after Hong Kong's new Chek Lap Kok airport opens next year.
"We want to improve our service and we see there is a demand for more capacity. We hope to be operating daily but we must go step by step and expand gradually," Moller Jensen said in an interview.
Because of the 12 hour, non stop flight by a 200-seat Boeing 767-300, only between four and five tonnes of belly cargo on average can be carried.

Moller Jensen said the additional passenger flight would complement the carrier's Boeing 747 Asian freighter service which calls at nearby Macau and, unusually, receives ex-Hong Kong freight by barge.
The general manager agreed that SAS now has a 'two-speed' cargo service with the faster cargo service provided by the Hong Kong passenger flights and the freighter service for larger loads via Macau.

"Our service into Macau is a valuable supplement to the passenger service from Hong Kong. We are getting good loads out of Hong Kong with a stable flow of cargo, especially textiles and garments," Moller Jensen added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
